q1.directions: Use the passage below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Describe ONE similarity between the American and French Revolutions in the period c. 1750 to c. 1900.
parts.b: Explain ONE difference between the American and French Revolutions, using the historian's interpretation in the passage.
parts.c: Explain ONE way in which Enlightenment ideas influenced revolutionary movements in the period c. 1750 to c. 1900.

sample_answers.a: Both revolutions overthrew monarchical authority in the name of popular sovereignty, replacing rule justified by divine right or tradition with governments claiming legitimacy from the consent of the governed.
sample_answers.b: According to the passage, the French Revolution attacked entrenched aristocratic privilege and the established church within its own society, producing deeper social upheaval, while the American Revolution mainly severed an imperial connection and left domestic social hierarchies largely intact.
sample_answers.c: Enlightenment writers argued that legitimate government rests on natural rights and the consent of the governed; revolutionaries in America and France cited these principles to justify resisting kings and drafting constitutions based on liberty and equality.

q1.stimulus:
Historians often compare the American and French Revolutions as twin expressions of an age of democratic revolution, yet they stress important differences between them. Both movements drew on Enlightenment ideas to challenge monarchical authority and claimed to act in the name of the people. However, the French Revolution confronted a deeply entrenched domestic order of aristocratic privilege and clerical power, and its attack on that order produced far-reaching social upheaval, including the destruction of feudal dues and the confiscation of church lands. The American Revolution, by contrast, was primarily a war of independence against a distant imperial government; once political separation was achieved, existing social and economic hierarchies within American society remained largely undisturbed, and institutions such as slavery persisted and even expanded.
—Historian's account of the Atlantic revolutions in the period c. 1750–1900

q2.directions: Use the passage below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Identify ONE Enlightenment principle expressed in the declaration.
parts.b: Describe ONE way in which the principles of the declaration challenged the old order in France.
parts.c: Explain ONE reason why the ideals of the declaration were not fully realized during the French Revolution.

sample_answers.a: The declaration expresses the principle that all men are born free and equal in rights, and that the aim of political association is to preserve natural rights including liberty, property, security, and resistance to oppression.
sample_answers.b: By declaring that sovereignty resides in the nation rather than in the king, and that social distinctions are valid only when founded on the general good, it directly undermined the divine-right monarchy and the legal privileges of the nobility and clergy.
sample_answers.c: The revolution's leaders suspended or violated these rights during crises such as the Terror, when thousands were executed without due process; additionally, the declaration's promise of equality was not extended to enslaved people in the colonies or to women, who remained excluded from political rights.

q2.stimulus:
Men are born and remain free and equal in rights. Social distinctions may be founded only upon the general good.

The aim of all political association is the preservation of the natural and imprescriptible rights of man. These rights are liberty, property, security, and resistance to oppression.

The principle of all sovereignty resides essentially in the nation. No body nor individual may exercise any authority which does not proceed directly from the nation.
—Declaration of the Rights of Man and of the Citizen, National Assembly of France, 1789

q3.directions: Use the image below to answer all parts of the question that follows.

parts.a: Describe ONE feature of the painting that connects it to revolutionary ideals of the period c. 1750 to c. 1900.
parts.b: Explain ONE way in which the painting reflects a continuity in French revolutionary symbolism between 1789 and 1830.
parts.c: Explain ONE difference between the revolution depicted in the painting and the American Revolution.

sample_answers.a: The central female figure of Liberty, wearing the Phrygian cap of freed slaves and carrying the French tricolor, personifies the revolutionary ideals of liberty and popular sovereignty triumphing over oppression.
sample_answers.b: The tricolor flag and the Phrygian cap were both symbols created during the 1789 revolution; their reappearance in a painting of the 1830 July Revolution shows that later French revolutionaries deliberately claimed the legacy and symbols of 1789 for their own struggle.
sample_answers.c: The painting shows a popular urban uprising with citizens of different classes fighting together on the barricades to overthrow a domestic king, whereas the American Revolution was a colonial war of independence fought against a distant British government rather than against France's own social order.

q3.stimulus: The image is Eugène Delacroix's 1830 oil painting Liberty Leading the People, commemorating the July Revolution of 1830 in Paris. A bare-breasted female figure personifying Liberty, wearing a Phrygian cap and holding the French tricolor flag, leads armed men of different social classes forward over a barricade strewn with the fallen. Though it depicts 1830, the painting deliberately uses the symbols of the 1789 French Revolution.

theme: Comparing the American and French Revolutions
